=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2908-2926, 18963-18977 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The main poller pre-filters state comments and short-circuits on identity failure before calling the extractor, preventing its filtered-comment and identity-unavailable diagnostics from running on that path.
  WHY: The tests expecting those diagnostics fail on the main poller path; severity is BLOCKER in qwen_qwen3_7-plus and z-ai_glm-5_2, but NIT in openai_gpt-6-luna.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2875-2889, 19010-19023 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Identity lookup failures can go without a Telegram alert when there are no active tracking issues, because the replacement alert is inside the per-issue loop and the prior alert in unblock_trusted_login was removed.
  WHY: On a no-tracking-issue cycle, the loop does not run and the standalone recovery and unblock scan paths do not notify operators; severity is MAJOR in minimax_minimax-m3 and qwen_qwen3_7-plus, but NIT in openai_gpt-6-luna and z-ai_glm-5_2.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~2918 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: EXTRACTED_STATE_UNTRUSTED_IGNORED is assigned the untrusted-comment count but is never read.
  WHY: The count is already emitted by the diagnostic above, while the unused variable adds dead state and could mislead a future caller.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:~1504 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The tightened confirmation condition no longer prompts for env -C or env -v wrapped commits, despite the test contract expecting those cases to be caught.
  WHY: With no resolved checkout, env -C /random/path git commit -m x can be silently allowed because env -C sets working_directory, not explicit_git_directory.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Before V1 or V2 extraction, accept state comments only from the verified pipeline identity; require every V2 chunk to meet that check and fail closed if identity cannot be established."
  expected_change_site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh extract_latest_valid_orchestrator_state() and all callers
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: The extractor-internal filtering at lines 2908-2926 is correct, but the main poller loop at line 18970 pre-filters comments before the extractor, so the extractor's per-chunk V2 author check (line 2934 passes trusted_comments_json to the V2 reader) is redundant on the main path. The security fix is complete for callers that don't pre-filter (resolve_active_orchestrator_context_for_issue at line 4724, run_standalone_stall_recovery at line 16805), but the main poller path relies on the pre-filter rather than the extractor, creating a dual-filtering inconsistency that breaks the tests.

=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~2875-2889 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The original `unblock_trusted_login` sent a one-shot CRITICAL Telegram alert whenever the `user` probe failed, but the replacement drops that alert; the new WARNING alert only runs inside the per-tracking-issue loop.
  WHY: When the GH_PAT identity probe fails on a tick with no active tracking issues, processing paths degrade without a Telegram alert; the severity downgrade also reduces urgency during a sustained identity outage.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~2918 | severity=NIT | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: `EXTRACTED_STATE_UNTRUSTED_IGNORED` is initialized to 0 and assigned the untrusted-comment count, but it is never read anywhere in the file or referenced by callers.
  WHY: The only diagnostic emission is the `outcome=filtered ignored=${ignored_count}` echo directly above; the unused variable adds noise and creates a maintenance trap.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~19010-19023 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The once-per-tick Telegram guard sits inside the per-tracking-issue `for` loop, so it does not fire when `COUNT==0`.
  WHY: A misconfigured `GH_PAT` on a quiet cycle produces only stdout `::warning::` lines and no Telegram alert.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:~1504 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The changed condition requires `config_override` OR `explicit_git_directory` alongside `warning`, so `env -C /does-not-exist git commit -m x` and `env -v git commit -m x` no longer match.
  WHY: An attacker who controls `cwd` could run `env -C /random/path git commit -m x` in a session that has no resolved checkout; the guard would silently allow the commit instead of asking for confirmation. `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:1440` still expects those cases to be caught.

=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2922-2925, 18970-18977 | severity=NIT | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The main poller filters comments to the trusted login before passing them to the extractor, so `ignored_count` cannot count forged comments; the `jq` expression used to compute `ignored_count` has an unclosed `select(`, its error is suppressed, and the fallback sets the count to zero.
  WHY: Forged state comments are excluded from extraction, but the promised `outcome=filtered` diagnostic is not emitted. The forged-state tests that assert this diagnostic fail on the main poller path.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2880-2887, 18965-18969, 16470-16474 | severity=NIT | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: When the GitHub identity lookup fails, the cached identity helper no longer sends the Telegram alert that its previous implementation sent.
  WHY: The main loop continues at 18969 before reaching the notification at 19015, and the unblock scan also returns after logging without notifying; identity failures are visible only in workflow logs on these paths.

=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:18970-18977, 2922-2926 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The main poller pre-filters comments into TRUSTED_STATE_COMMENTS before passing them to extract_latest_valid_orchestrator_state, so the extractor's internal filtering never sees untrusted comments on the main processing path.
  WHY: The tests test_state_extraction_ignores_newer_forged_state and test_state_extraction_skips_mixed_author_v2_chain check for "outcome=filtered" in stderr, but on the main poller path, ignored_count will always be 0 because the extractor receives only pre-filtered trusted comments.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~2879, ~19013-19018 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The old unblock_trusted_login() definition sent a CRITICAL Telegram alert when the identity probe failed, but the replacement alert is only sent inside the main tracking-issue loop.
  WHY: When there are no tracking issues (COUNT=0), the main loop does not run, run_standalone_stall_recovery() at line 16808-16810 detects EXTRACTED_STATE_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE=true and returns silently with only a stdout warning, and run_unblock_scan() at line 24843 also proceeds without any Telegram alert.

  WHY: When COUNT=0, run_standalone_stall_recovery silently returns at line 16808 and run_unblock_scan proceeds without any Telegram alert, reducing operator visibility.

The security fix is complete for callers that don't pre-filter (resolve_active_orchestrator_context_for_issue at line 4724, run_standalone_stall_recovery at line 16805), but the main poller path relies on the pre-filter rather than the extractor, creating a dual-filtering inconsistency that breaks the tests.
